sentence: Each hand consists of 27 bones: eight carpal bones in the wrist, five metacarpal bones forming the palm and fourteen phalanges in the thumb and fingers.
note: StatPearls: each hand has 27 bones. OpenStax: eight carpals in two rows, five metacarpals forming the palm, fourteen phalanges.

sentence: The carpal bones lie in two rows of four, and only the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum take part in the wrist joint with the radius.
note: OpenStax: proximal and distal rows of four carpals; only the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum take part in the wrist joint with the radius.

sentence: The scaphoid is the carpal bone most often fractured, typically after a fall onto the hand.
note: OpenStax: scaphoid is the most frequently fractured carpal bone, often after a fall onto the hand; StatPearls: most commonly injured carpal bone.

sentence: 27: eight carpals, five metacarpals and fourteen phalanges
note: StatPearls: each hand has 27 bones; OpenStax: eight carpals, five metacarpals, fourteen phalanges.

sentence: Scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum and pisiform, counting from the thumb side
note: OpenStax and StatPearls: proximal row from the thumb (radial) side is scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform.

sentence: Trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate, counting from the thumb side
note: OpenStax and StatPearls: distal row from the thumb (radial) side is trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

sentence: Scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum articulate with the radius
note: OpenStax: only three proximal carpals, the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum, take part in the wrist joint with the radius.

sentence: The thumb has two phalanges; each of the other four digits has three
note: OpenStax and StatPearls: thumb has proximal and distal phalanges; digits 2 to 5 have proximal, middle (intermediate) and distal phalanges.

sentence: Roofed by the flexor retinaculum; carries nine flexor tendons and the median nerve
note: StatPearls: flexor retinaculum forms the anterior roof; four superficialis, four profundus and one flexor pollicis longus tendon plus the median nerve lie deep to it.

sentence: X-ray first; a scaphoid fracture can be hard to see at first, so a repeat X-ray or an MRI scan may follow
note: Trust leaflets: scaphoid fracture may not show on first X-ray; examination and X-ray repeated later; MRI requested if suspicion continues.

sentence: The eight carpal bones make up the wrist, the five metacarpal bones form the palm and the fourteen phalanges form the thumb and fingers.
note: StatPearls: eight wrist (carpal) bones; OpenStax: five metacarpals form the palm, fourteen phalanges per hand; StatPearls: 27 bones per hand.

sentence: The metacarpals are numbered one to five starting from the thumb, and each is associated with a group of phalanges.
note: OpenStax: metacarpals numbered 1 to 5 from the thumb side; StatPearls: each metacarpal is associated with a group of phalanges.

sentence: The first metacarpal is freely mobile, whereas the other metacarpals are united as a group.
note: OpenStax: the first metacarpal bone is freely mobile, but the other metacarpal bones are united as a group.

sentence: The thumb has only two phalanges, a proximal and a distal, while each of the other four digits, from the index finger to the little finger, has a proximal, middle and distal phalanx.
note: OpenStax: thumb has proximal and distal phalanges; digits 2 (index) to 5 (little) have proximal, middle and distal phalanges. StatPearls agrees.

sentence: The knuckles are the metacarpophalangeal joints, where each metacarpal meets the proximal phalanx of its digit.
note: OpenStax: knuckles are the metacarpophalangeal joints, where each metacarpal meets the proximal phalanx of its digit.

sentence: The eight carpal bones are arranged in two rows of four, a proximal row and a distal row.
note: OpenStax: carpal bones form a proximal row of four and a distal row of four; StatPearls: eight carpals in two rows.

sentence: Counting from the thumb side, the proximal row is the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum and pisiform, and the distal row is the trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate.
note: OpenStax and StatPearls list the proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate) from the thumb side.

sentence: Several names describe shape: scaphoid means boat-shaped, lunate moon-shaped, triquetrum three-cornered, pisiform pea-shaped, capitate head-shaped and hamate hooked.
note: OpenStax glosses scaphoid boat-shaped, lunate moon-shaped, triquetrum three-cornered, pisiform pea-shaped, capitate head-shaped, hamate hooked bone.

sentence: The pisiform can be felt as a bony bump at the medial base of the hand, and the hamate has a prominent bony extension on its anterior side, the hook of the hamate.
note: OpenStax: pisiform is the bony bump felt at the medial base of the hand; hamate has a prominent anterior extension, the hook of the hamate.

sentence: Only the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum take part in the wrist joint with the radius.
note: OpenStax: only three proximal bones, the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum, take part in the wrist joint with the radius.

sentence: The flexor retinaculum, a fibrous band often called the transverse carpal ligament, forms the anterior roof of the carpal tunnel at the wrist.
note: StatPearls: fibrous band forming the anterior roof of the tunnel; flexor retinaculum and transverse carpal ligament are often used interchangeably.

sentence: Deep to the band lie the four flexor digitorum superficialis tendons, the four flexor digitorum profundus tendons, the flexor pollicis longus tendon and the median nerve.
note: StatPearls lists four flexor digitorum superficialis, four flexor digitorum profundus and the flexor pollicis longus tendons plus the median nerve deep to the ligament.

sentence: Carpal tunnel syndrome is compression of the median nerve at the wrist, causing hand pain, numbness and tingling in the area the nerve supplies.
note: Review: carpal tunnel syndrome is median nerve compression at the wrist, with hand pain, numbness and tingling in the nerve territory.

sentence: In longer-standing cases the muscle at the base of the thumb can waste.
note: Review: in longer-standing cases muscle wasting at the base of the thumb can develop.

sentence: Thickening of the transverse carpal ligament and swelling of the tendons narrow the space and can compress the nerve, although in most cases the cause is unknown.
note: Review: thickening of the transverse carpal ligament and tendon swelling narrow the space and compress the nerve; in most cases the cause is unknown.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: The scaphoid is the most frequently fractured carpal bone, and NHS trust leaflets describe it as a small bone at the base of the thumb.
note: OpenStax: most frequently fractured carpal bone; trust page: a small bone at the base of the thumb, the most common wrist bone to break.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: A fall onto an outstretched hand is described as the most common cause of both scaphoid injuries and wrist fractures.
note: Trust leaflets: a fall onto an outstretched hand is the most common cause of a scaphoid injury and of wrist fractures.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: A scaphoid injury typically causes pain and tenderness near the base of the thumb, and the wrist may swell, but most scaphoid fractures do not make the wrist look broken and many cause only minor symptoms.
note: Trust leaflets: pain and tenderness near the thumb base, possible swelling; most do not make the wrist look broken, many cause minor symptoms.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: Some people also have difficulty gripping or twisting the wrist or thumb.
note: Trust leaflets: some people also have trouble gripping or twisting the wrist or thumb.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: NHS trust pages on wrist fractures describe immediate severe pain, swelling and often deformity of the wrist, painful movement, and sometimes tingling or numbness in the fingers.
note: Trust wrist-fracture pages: immediate severe pain, swelling and often deformity; movement often painful; fingers sometimes tingly or numb.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: Wrist fractures are common in young children and older people.
note: Trust wrist-fracture summary: wrist fractures are common in young children and older people.

where: section:Fractures of the wrist and scaphoid
sentence: A wrist sprain can cause similar symptoms, and some suspected scaphoid injuries turn out to be sprains or bone bruises rather than breaks.
note: Trust leaflets: sprains cause similar symptoms; some suspected scaphoid injuries turn out to be sprains or bone bruises; imaging tells them apart.

sentence: A scaphoid fracture can be hard to diagnose because a stable fracture may be only a thin crack that is difficult to see on X-ray.
note: Trust leaflets: a stable scaphoid fracture may be a thin crack that is difficult to see on X-ray.

sentence: In some people the fracture is not obvious on X-ray until some days after the injury.
note: Trust leaflets: in some cases a scaphoid fracture is not obvious on X-ray until some days (around ten to fourteen) after the injury.

sentence: When the first X-ray is normal but a fracture is still suspected, clinicians re-examine the wrist and repeat the X-ray, and an MRI scan is requested if suspicion continues.
note: Trust leaflets: if the first X-ray is normal but suspicion remains, the wrist is re-examined and X-rayed again; MRI is requested if suspicion continues.

sentence: Even without a visible fracture, a doctor who suspects one from the symptoms may treat the wrist as fractured to avoid complications.
note: Trust leaflets: if a fracture is suspected from symptoms, it may be treated as a fracture even when not visible, to avoid complications.

sentence: An X-ray is a quick, painless test that produces images of the inside of the body; the person needs to keep still, and more than one image may be taken from different angles.
note: Northampton General leaflet: X-ray is quick and painless; keep still so the image is not blurred; several images from different angles may be taken.
